messages:
kevin: Heads-up — sales forwarded a request from a private/VPC customer. They block egress to external model hosts but want a 'best-effort' fallback to a local quantized variant when hosted routing is disallowed. Can our routing policy express this?

maira: Do they want the control plane to decide the fallback, or should the tenant preconfigure a local variant?

kevin: Prefer control-plane-driven if possible — customer doesn't want to manage models. But they do want an audit reason for every time we switch to local.

raj: Two concerns: 1) security/egress rules — if VPC forbids outbound, control plane shouldn't try crossing the wire. 2) licensing/data residency — fallback must respect allowed regions.

sophia: Agreed. We can gate external routing with a policy flag on the tenant: `egress_policy: allow|deny|restricted`. If deny => never call external models. If restricted => allow cross-region only for enterprise tier.

maira: UX question — what does the console show when a request hits the policy? We should surface the reason code so customers understand behavior (not just a 502).

kevin: Proposal: extend routing decision payload with two fields in telemetry: `route.decision` (hosted/local/blocked) and `fallback.reason` (policy/latency/capacity). Console uses these for rollout graphs.

sophia: We also need to ensure logs are privacy-safe when it's a private tenant — redact request text in traces and only surface token counts and model ids.

raj: Small config sketch for policy (for discussion):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  egress_policy: deny
  fallback:
    enabled: true
    mode: control_plane
    local_variant: redwood-quant-7b
    tier_overrides:
      enterprise: allow_cross_region
      standard: deny_cross_region
```

kevin: That looks good. Important: if `egress_policy: deny` then `allow_cross_region` should be ignored unless tenant explicitly opts in via signed agreement. 

maira: For the console, show deterministic behavior: if blocked, button says "Fallback active — local model" with tooltip showing `fallback.reason: policy_block` and link to tenant settings. :information_source:

ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled a canary for routing-service-v2 tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Will test policy matrix for 3 tenants.

kevin: Telemetry requirements for the rollout: capture counts per minute for decisions, percent of requests using local_variant, and histogram of latency delta (hosted vs local). Also require sampling of 0.1% request payload hashes for debug (redacted).

maira: Who owns adding the tier override behavior + console exposure?

raj: I'll take routing-policy config + server-side enforcement. Assigning to @raj.

maira: I'll own console UX + docs.

kevin: @sophia can you add the telemetry redaction rules and the trace fields?

sophia: Yep. I'll add `route.decision`, `fallback.reason`, `policy.violated`, and `tenant.region` fields. Will make sure we don't log request text for private tenants.

kevin: One edge case: what if fallback local_variant isn't available on the tenant's dedicated pool (capacity)? Should we surface an explicit error or queue a job to warm the local model?

raj: We should prefer graceful degradation: if local_variant not present, respond with a structured error that includes `fallback.reason: capacity_missing` and `suggested_action: warm_local_variant`. Queue warming as async and track warm attempts in console.

maira: UX: show warm status in tenant detail page with timestamps + last attempted warm. Also allow manual warm-from-console.

kevin: OK action list: 1) raj -> implement policy flags + enforcement endpoints (PR) 2) sophia -> telemetry schema + redaction rules 3) maira -> console strings, warm UI 4) kevin -> coordinate docs and enterprise consent flow. We'll validate during canary.

deploy-bot: canary plan created: routing-policy-canary-193245 on infra-staging with 3 tenants, 1000 reqs/min, duration 2h.

kevin: Thanks. Let's sync after canary. If any of you hit blockers ping #eng-oncall.

sophia: noted. I'll draft telemetry PR today.

raj: starting policy server work now, will post RFC link in thread.

maira: I'll mock console screens and link them here by EOD.

kevin: Great. :thumbsup:
